fields.title: The Fed's rate is 4.75% or higher after its April 28, 2027 meeting
fields.text: The upper bound of the federal funds target range stands at 4.75% or higher after the FOMC meeting that ends April 28, 2027: at least three more quarter-point rises from today's 3.75%-4.00% across the December, January, March and April meetings. April's is the last meeting inside the horizon.

chances.note: If the Fed raises in December, January and March the rate is already 4.75% after March; it stays at or above that unless April brings a cut. Polymarket's April-decision market puts a cut at about 12% unconditionally, and a cut one meeting after three straight rises is less likely than that, so 0.92.

Without three straight rises, 4.75% by April needs two rises by March and another in April, or a half-point step. Polymarket's parlay puts two-of-three paths (Hike-Hike-Pause, Hike-Pause-Hike) at about 0.53 of all paths, 0.80 of the paths that are not Hike-Hike-Hike; an April rise is priced near 0.24. 0.80 x 0.24 is 0.19.

to.title: The Fed's rate is 5.00% or higher after April: a rise at every meeting, or a half-point step
to.text: The upper bound of the federal funds target range stands at 5.00% or higher after the FOMC meeting that ends April 28, 2027: four or more quarter points from today, which takes a rise at each of the four meetings or a half-point move.

to.title: The Fed's rate is 4.75% after April: three more rises
to.text: The upper bound of the federal funds target range stands at exactly 4.75% after the FOMC meeting that ends April 28, 2027.

to.title: The Fed's rate is 4.50% after April: two more rises
to.text: The upper bound of the federal funds target range stands at exactly 4.50% after the FOMC meeting that ends April 28, 2027: December's rise and one more.

to.title: The Fed's rate is 4.25% or lower after April: the rises stop after December, or reverse
to.text: The upper bound of the federal funds target range stands at 4.25% or lower after the FOMC meeting that ends April 28, 2027: at most one more rise net, because inflation cools quickly or because growth or markets crack.

markets.question: Will the upper bound of the federal funds rate be above 4.50% following the Fed's Apr 28, 2027 meeting?
markets.family: Fed funds rate after Apr 2027 meeting?
markets.rules:
If the upper bound of the target federal funds rate published on the Federal Reserve's official website is greater than 4.50% following the Federal Reserve's Apr 28, 2027 meeting, then the market resolves to Yes.

This market will expire the first 2:05 PM ET following the release of a Federal Reserve statement for their Apr 28, 2027 meeting or one week following the last day of that meeting.

markets.question: Will the Fed hike-hike-hike in the next three decisions (Dec-Jan-Mar)?
markets.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds rate. The decisions on the target federal funds rate are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 8 to 9, 2026; January 26 to 27, 2027; and March 16 to 17, 2027.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate moves are explicitly excluded from this market. Any hike or cut to the target federal funds rate announced outside the three regularly scheduled meetings listed above, including at any unscheduled or emergency FOMC meeting, will not be considered and will not count as one of the three decisions. Each scheduled meeting's decision is measured against the upper bound in effect immediately before that meeting, including any emergency change made since the previous meeting, regardless of whether the scheduled decision reverses an emergency change.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
